findings.claim: James Watt-Smith (Gousto), Sophie Trelawney (Trinny London) and James Watt (BrewDog) all left comfortable jobs because they backed their idea.
findings.truth: Gousto was founded in 2012 by Timo Boldt and James Carter. Trinny London was founded in 2017 by Trinny Woodall. 'James Watt-Smith' and 'Sophie Trelawney' do not exist. James Watt (BrewDog) is real.

findings.claim: For calculation questions involving opportunity cost, always name the alternative that was sacrificed
findings.truth: Opportunity cost is a defined term in spec 3.1.1 but is not a calculation. The examinable calculations are listed in spec 6.1: revenue, costs and profit, percentages and percentage change, averages, gross and net profit margin, average rate of return, cash flow forecasts.

findings.claim: Students may also pick one factor and develop it in depth, as the 2026 assessment approach allows.
findings.truth: There is no '2026 assessment approach'. The specification is version 1.0 (2016), for exams from 2019, and it is unchanged. This is an invented assessment claim inside a mark scheme.

findings.claim: When Aston Martin floated as a Plc in 2018, the founders accepted public scrutiny of every quarterly result
findings.truth: Aston Martin was founded in 1913 by Lionel Martin and Robert Bamford. The October 2018 flotation was carried out by the company's then owners, an investor consortium. The founders had no part in it.

findings.claim: A partnership has between 2 and 20 owners (repeated in the glossary, one flashcard definition, the flashcard 'What is the maximum number of partners in a standard partnership?' answered '20 partners', and knowledge check 2 which marks '20' correct).
findings.truth: The 20-member cap was removed by the Regulatory Reform (Removal of 20 Member Limit in Partnerships etc.) Order 2002. UK partnerships have had no legal maximum since December 2002. The Partnership Act 1890 never set one. The choice is between legal accuracy and the '2 to 20' convention still printed in many GCSE textbooks; the specification is silent on numbers, so no marks turn on it either way. Recommended ruling: change every '2-20' to 'two or more', reword knowledge check 2 to 'Since 2002, how many partners can a UK partnership legally have?' with correct index 3 ('Unlimited'), and reword the max-partners flashcard to state that the limit was removed in 2002.
findings.evidence: legislation.gov.uk: Regulatory Reform (Removal of 20 Member Limit in Partnerships etc.) Order 2002 (SI 2002/3203)
findings.ruling: 20-partner cap removed (SI 2002/3203): content dfn+prose, two flashcards, glossary, KC2 stem+key updated to 'two or more / no legal maximum'.

findings.claim: diseconomies of scale and cash-flow strain are real risks (see Patisserie Valerie collapse)
findings.truth: Patisserie Valerie went into administration in January 2019 as a direct result of accounting fraud. A roughly 20 million pound discrepancy and unreported overdrafts were found in October 2018, and four people were charged in 2023. It is not an example of diseconomies of scale.

findings.claim: Unilever reports on its Sustainable Living brands
findings.truth: The Unilever Sustainable Living Plan ran to 2020 and was replaced by the Unilever Compass. The present tense is dated rather than wrong, and no marks depend on it.

findings.claim: Students may develop one factor in depth per the 2026 approach.
when Boohoo was linked to underpaid factory workers in Leicester, sales fell and the share price halved
findings.truth: Boohoo's sales rose. First-quarter revenue was up 45% and the group's full-year revenue grew strongly through 2020-21. The share price did fall about 46% in July 2020 after the Leicester allegations.

findings.claim: For a co-operative like John Lewis, employees are the owners.
findings.truth: John Lewis Partnership is not a co-operative. It is a public limited company owned by a trust on behalf of all its employees, an employee-ownership structure set up by Spedan Lewis in 1950.

findings.claim: Draws on 2026 approach allowing multiple factors with developed reasoning.
Morrisons' 2005 takeover of Safeway instantly doubled its store network.
findings.truth: The Safeway takeover completed in March 2004. Safeway owned 479 stores, against roughly 125 for Morrisons, so the network grew far more than double before divestments.

findings.claim: diseconomies of scale raise average unit cost when firms overstretch (Patisserie Valerie, parts of M&S)
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F6. Patisserie Valerie collapsed because of accounting fraud, not overstretching.

summary: Every practice tariff (1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12), paper claim and calculation checks out, and all 30 knowledge-check keys are correct. The damage is three invented '2026 assessment approach' claims planted in mark schemes, two fabricated entrepreneur names, and five wrong real-world facts (Boohoo sales, Morrisons/Safeway year, Aston Martin founders, John Lewis as a co-operative, Patisserie Valerie blamed on diseconomies of scale twice).
